facts.raw_span: A man in his 60s presented with an enlarging purpuric patch on his left lateral superior forehead and left anterior scalp
initially present for 2 weeks
the lesion first developed in March 2014 and was fairly stable until June 2014
rapid growth and extension followed by central ulceration and bleeding
a 30 × 25-cm centrally eroded purpuric plaque with multifocal peripheral reddish-purple patches, papules, and macules
involving: Left anterior scalp with extension posteriorly on left parietal scalp
No evidence of lymphadenopathy in preauricular, cervical, occipital, submandibular or supraclavicular areas
Dermis permeated by irregular, slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes and lined by plump oval cells
Cells had pale eosinophilic cytoplasm and hyperchromatic nuclei
Cells stained positively with CD31 and were negative for CK5
No evidence of nodal, pulmonary, or liver metastases
Staging: T2N0M0

concepts.why: The presence of a large, centrally eroded purpuric plaque with multifocal peripheral reddish-purple patches, papules, and macules, along with the histopathological findings of irregular, slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes and lined by plump oval cells, suggests Angiosarcoma.

The clinical presentation of a purpuric patch with rapid growth and extension, along with the histopathological findings of slitlike spaces and plump oval cells, could be consistent with Kaposi's Sarcoma.

The presence of a large, purpuric plaque with multifocal peripheral reddish-purple patches, papules, and macules, could be suggestive of a Hemangioma, although the aggressive behavior and histopathological findings are not typical.
The combination of clinical and histopathological findings, including the presence of irregular, slitlike spaces and plump oval cells, could be consistent with Malignant Hemangioendothelioma.

The clinical presentation of a large, purpuric plaque with multifocal peripheral reddish-purple patches, papules, and macules, could be suggestive of Poikiloderma Vasculare Atrophicans, although the aggressive behavior and histopathological findings are not typical.
The staging of T2N0M0, as indicated by the imaging studies, is consistent with a localized angiosarcoma of the scalp, which explains the enlarging purpuric patch and rapid growth of the lesion.

rationales.F05: A large, centrally eroded purpuric plaque with multifocal peripheral reddish-purple patches, papules, and macules is highly suggestive of angiosarcoma and malignant hemangioendothelioma.
rationales.F08: The presence of irregular, slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes and lined by plump oval cells is highly characteristic of angiosarcoma and malignant hemangioendothelioma.
rationales.F09: Cells with pale eosinophilic cytoplasm and hyperchromatic nuclei are more typical of angiosarcoma and malignant hemangioendothelioma.
rationales.F10: Positive staining for CD31 and negative staining for CK5 is more characteristic of angiosarcoma and malignant hemangioendothelioma.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's presentation with a rapidly growing, centrally eroded purpuric plaque on the scalp, along with the histopathological findings of irregular, slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes and cells staining positively with CD31, strongly supports a diagnosis of angiosarcoma. The specific location on the scalp and the staging of T2N0M0 further specify the diagnosis to Angiosarcoma of the scalp.
